inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report cash-flow reconciliation 'Share-based payments 6.0' (FY2025 10.7; RHC.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:8398). Group figure, taken wholly against the Funding Group. No equity-award tax line (EquityAwardTaxes 0 in every year). Forward path uses 0.08% of revenue, the FY2025-26 average, rather than the low FY2026 print.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted average, FY2026 EPS note (230.8m; basic 230.2m). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, and the DRP was suspended from the FY2025 final dividend. The 2.6m CARES preference shares are NOT in the count; they are deducted at face in the equity bridge instead.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-13T05:10:12Z regular ASX close (Yahoo Finance chart API)
inputs.net_debt_basis: FUNDING GROUP ONLY (Ramsay ex Ramsay Sante). 1,912.8 Funding Group net debt excl. lease liabilities and derivatives at 30 June 2026 (FY2026 AR section 3.2.2) + 251.0 net acquisition price of National Capital Private Hospital, completed 31 August 2026 after balance date (H1 FY2026 report line 792; FY2026 AR note 20). Ramsay Sante's ~2.65bn of non-recourse net debt is excluded because Sante is carried in the equity bridge at market value, not in the flows. The annual report does not split Funding Group gross borrowings from cash, so total_debt and cash are deliberately omitted rather than guessed (consolidated: borrowings 5,293.8, cash 729.9).
inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.0%, built in AUD: risk-free ~4.4% (10-year ACGB), equity risk premium ~5.75%, beta ~0.8 for a defensive hospital operator -> cost of equity ~9.0%; pre-tax cost of debt 5.5% (management's FY27 Funding Group guidance) -> ~3.9% after tax; ~15% debt weight on market values with leases treated as operating cost. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is carried in the flows and the weights, not the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. The full Funding Group lease cash cost is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path and lease liabilities (Funding Group 2,218.6) are EXCLUDED from net debt. FY2026 lease cash ~250 = 149.9 AASB16 lease finance cost (disclosed, section 3.2.1) + ~100 principal (ESTIMATE: the Funding Group principal is not disclosed; group principal is 592.1, and the Funding Group's 'other financing cash flows' of -108.4 with roughly flat borrowings brackets it at ~100). D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (Funding Group underlying D&A 423 less ~115 estimated ROU depreciation = ~308, 3.3% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice. The ~25m uncertainty on principal/ROU split is worth roughly $1/share.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, by construction: essentially all group NCI sits in Ramsay Sante (47.21% minority), which is valued only at Ramsay's 52.79% share of market capitalisation in the equity bridge. Funding Group NCI is immaterial and ignored.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF on the FUNDING GROUP (Australia + UK acute + Elysium) plus Ramsay Sante at market in the equity bridge, a sum-of-parts. Reason: Ramsay is an operating hospital company (routing row 'operating company, non-US' + adaptations), but consolidated figures blend in a 52.79%-owned, separately financed, separately listed French subsidiary that is about to leave the group. Shareholders vote on 24 November 2026 on an in-specie distribution of the whole Sante stake, with implementation expected mid-December 2026; Sante will be a discontinued operation in the FY27 accounts and all FY27 guidance is given for the Funding Group only. Valuing the consolidated flows would capitalise Sante's EBITDA at an Australian hospital multiple and then need a 47% NCI haircut and 2.65bn of Sante debt; valuing the stake at its Euronext price avoids all three. CURRENT PRICE IS CUM-DISTRIBUTION: once the demerger is implemented the RHC price falls by the value of the Sante shares handed out (about $3.46/share at current marks) and the 'Ramsay Sante stake' bridge item must be REMOVED on the next update, or the stake is counted in a company that no longer owns it. If the vote fails, the item stays. BASE REVENUE 9,399 = Funding Group segment revenue and other income 9,423.1 less 24.1 of disposal gains (HotDoc 14.0, Elysium site restructure 10.1). EBITDA margin anchor: Funding Group underlying EBITDA 1,254.8 (Australia 902.6 + UK 352.2) = 13.3%, post-AASB16; the lease charge is then deducted separately. reported_fcf 282.4 = Funding Group free cash flow 382.4 (after all finance costs and tax, section 3.2.2) less the ~100 estimated lease principal; last_fcf is therefore a LEVERED FY2026 figure shown for reference, while the projections are unlevered. FY2026 Funding Group cash flow was helped by a +12.1 working-capital inflow and +49.3 of other items. Continuing operations throughout: the Dec-2023 Ramsay Sime Darby sale (618.1 gain in FY2024) and the 305.2 UK impairment in FY2025 are outside the base year and outside underlying EBITDA. SBC is tiny (0.06% of revenue), so the house and street values nearly coincide and band_position carries no information for this ticker. Buybacks: none since FY2020; the flat count is a convention funded implicitly by the SBC charge. Undrawn demerger transaction costs beyond the 16m booked to 30 June 2026 are not deducted (amount in the scheme booklet, which is not in the research folder). Analysis JSON did not exist at build time; scenario axes are drawn from the FY2026 Annual Report.

equity_bridge.note: 110,389,690 Ramsay Generale de Sante shares x 52.79% = 58.27m shares x EUR 8.42 (GDS.PA close 2026-11-13, at its 52-week low; range 8.42-11.55) x EUR/AUD 1.6272 (Yahoo EURAUD=X 2026-11-14). Carrying value in the Funding Group balance sheet is 837.4. Thinly traded: free float is small, so the mark is indicative. REMOVE after the in-specie distribution is implemented (expected mid-December 2026).

2.6m Convertible Adjustable Rate Equity Securities x $100 face (book 252.2 in equity, FY2026 AR note 6.c). Redeemable or convertible at Ramsay's election; dividends of 15.7 a year rank ahead of ordinary holders and are not in the unlevered flows.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (4.2%) is more than 30% below revenue CAGR (7.6%) and EPS has shrunk (-6.8% a year over five years): revenue growth since FY2021 came with margin compression, the Elysium acquisition and a 305m impairment, not with per-share value creation.
historical_growth.notes: All CAGRs are CONSOLIDATED (including Ramsay Sante), FY2021/FY2023 to FY2026, statutory EPS. The FCF series is reported free cash flow less SBC; it is struck BEFORE lease principal (592.1 in FY2026 against 696.5 of reported FCF), so consolidated reported FCF overstates owner cash flow by most of its value and its CAGR should not be read as an owner-FCF trend. No consistent Funding Group owner-FCF history exists before FY2025. Funding Group revenue grew 4.9% in FY2026 (Australia +7.8%, UK -2.1%).

base.growth_note: Year 1: Australia ~+6.5% organic (FY2026 +7.8%) plus ten months of National Capital, UK ~+1.5% (NHS indexation 1.24%, Elysium beds down 9.8%).
base.margin_note: FY2026 underlying 13.3%. Guidance is EBIT growth and margin improvement in FY27 in Australia and both UK businesses. Path adds 1.3pp over eight years; pre-AASB16 EBIT margin goes 7.4% -> ~8.6%, still far below the ~13% Australian EBIT margins of FY2019.
base.capex_note: Year 1 = 5.1% (~510) inside the 480-520 Funding Group guidance. Fades to 4.0% as the Australian brownfield program slows; maintenance plus IT is ~270-300 today, so 4.0% leaves ~0.6pp of growth capex above D&A in perpetuity.
base.tax_note: Management guides ~30% Funding Group underlying rate (FY2026 29.4%).
base.wc_note: Negative: Funding Group working capital is +496 on 9.4bn of revenue (receivables exceed payables), so growth consumes cash.

scenario_narratives.base: The FY2026 recovery continues at a measured pace. Australian admissions grow 2-3% a year with rising acuity, and private health insurer indexation keeps up with nurse wage inflation rather than beating it, so the margin gain comes from theatre utilisation, procurement and revenue-cycle work, partly reinvested in the extra $10-15m a year of IT spend. National Capital is integrated as guided. The Joondalup public contract stays a drag at its new funding level. UK acute holds NHS volume losses to low single digits and keeps shifting to private pay (27% of admissions); Elysium's turnaround lifts it from a 3% to a mid-single-digit EBIT margin on a smaller bed base. Funding Group EBITDA margin rises from 13.3% to 14.6%, well short of pre-2020 levels, and capex eases from 5.1% to 4.0% of revenue as the brownfield program slows.
scenario_narratives.bull: Australian private hospital funding is reset. Insurers concede indexation above cost inflation after the Healthscope collapse removed capacity and bargaining weight from the sector, and Ramsay takes share of the displaced surgical volume; day-surgery centres and robotics lift throughput on the existing estate. UK NHS waiting-list policy turns back to the independent sector and private-pay growth continues; Elysium reaches high-single-digit margins as agency labour is eliminated and surplus sites are sold. EBITDA margin recovers to 16.5%, roughly two-thirds of the way back to the pre-COVID level, and the UK lease burden falls as a share of revenue.
scenario_narratives.bear: Margins roll over again, as they did in FY2022-FY2025. State nursing agreements and minimum-wage rises (UK National Living Wage, National Insurance) outrun payor indexation; insurers push more work into out-of-hospital and day settings and resist rate increases; NHS budget constraint deepens (FY2026 NHS volumes were already down 8.2%) and private pay does not fill the gap; Elysium occupancy falls faster than beds can be closed and further impairments follow. Fixed-uplift UK leases rise as a share of slower revenue. EBITDA margin drifts to 12.3% and capex stays elevated because the maintenance backlog cannot be deferred in a clinical estate. No covenant stress at this path: Funding Group leverage is 1.83x against a 2.5x target.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25%, above the 15% house default: two payor groups (Australian private health insurers and the NHS) set most of the price, and the bear path is simply a repeat of what happened to margins in FY2022-FY2025, not a tail event; balance-sheet risk is low at 1.83x Funding Group leverage, which is why it is not higher. Base 50%: management's FY27 guidance (EBIT and margin growth in all three Funding Group businesses) and two halves of delivery support it. Bull 25%, below the 35% default: it needs an insurer funding reset in Australia AND an NHS volume recovery AND an Elysium turnaround, three largely independent things.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Ramsay is valued as what it will be after mid-December 2026: an Australian private hospital operator with a UK acute and mental-health business, plus a parcel of Ramsay Sante shares marked at the Euronext price until they are distributed. The Funding Group is a low-margin, capital-heavy, lease-heavy business whose value is almost entirely a margin-recovery question: every 1pp of EBITDA margin in the terminal year is worth roughly $6-7 a share. The house model charges the full cash lease bill and the full development capex, which is why owner free cash flow is about 3% of revenue against a reported consolidated 'free cash flow' that looks more than twice as rich.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin path dominates: the spread between bear (12.3%) and bull (16.5%) terminal EBITDA margin is most of the spread in value, and it is set by payor indexation versus wage inflation, which Ramsay does not control.
Lease estimate: Funding Group lease principal (~100) and right-of-use depreciation (~115) are estimated because only consolidated figures are disclosed; a 25m error is worth about $1 a share.

Ramsay Sante mark: the stake is valued at a thinly traded price sitting at its 52-week low; it is $3.46 of the per-share value and leaves the company in mid-December 2026 if shareholders approve the distribution on 24 November.
Capex fade: the base case assumes capex falls from 5.1% to 4.0% of revenue. If Australian brownfield spending stays at FY2026 levels the base value is materially lower.
Terminal value is capped at 18x unlevered owner FCF and carries the bulk of enterprise value in every scenario.
Net debt is as at 30 June 2026 adjusted only for the National Capital purchase; the 48.5c final dividend paid since is not deducted.
